violations.description: This OSCE collection contains 52 scenarios but NONE require radiology interpretation expertise. All scenarios are clinical assessment stations (history taking, physical examination, management), not imaging interpretation stations.
violations.recommendation: This content should be evaluated by clinical experts (history-taking-expert, physical-examination-expert, clinical-documentation-expert), NOT radiology-interpretation-expert.

violations.description: All 'clinical_images' are placeholders with non-existent file paths (data/images/...). No actual radiological images provided for interpretation. File paths like 'data/images/endocrinology/hyperthyroidism_osce.jpg' do not exist and cannot be evaluated for systematic interpretation, image quality, or technical adequacy.
violations.recommendation: If radiology interpretation is intended, replace placeholders with actual imaging files (DICOM, JPG of real CXRs/ECGs/CTs). Currently 0/52 stations have interpretable images.

violations.description: Many listed 'image types' are not radiological investigations: 'Thyroid_Function_Tests' (laboratory), 'ABG_Glucose' (laboratory), 'Glucose_Chart' (clinical data), 'Neurological_Exam' (physical examination), 'Assessment_Form' (clinical documentation), 'Bristol_Stool_Chart' (clinical tool), 'Dix_Hallpike' (clinical maneuver). These are NOT imaging modalities.
violations.recommendation: Remove non-imaging content from radiology evaluation. Laboratory results, physical examination findings, and clinical assessment forms are outside radiology scope.

violations.description: OSCE scenarios provide NO radiological images to interpret systematically. Cannot apply ABCDE (CXR), 7-step ECG, or ABC (CT) methods when no images exist. Scenarios are clinical vignettes ('Patient presenting with Hyperthyroidism... Assess and manage'), not imaging interpretation tasks.
violations.recommendation: For radiology OSCE stations, task must be 'Interpret this CXR/ECG/CT' with actual image provided, NOT 'Assess and manage [condition]'.

violations.description: No technical imaging details provided: projection (PA/AP for CXR), window settings (brain/bone for CT), calibration (10mm/mV for ECG), patient positioning, clinical indication for imaging. Cannot assess image quality without these parameters.
violations.location: All OSCEs with radiological image types (37/52)
violations.recommendation: Add: 1) Technical parameters (kVp, mAs for X-ray; slice thickness for CT; ECG calibration); 2) Clinical indication ('72-year-old with sudden-onset chest pain - rule out MI'); 3) Previous imaging for comparison.

violations.description: References are general textbooks (John Murtagh General Practice, Churchill's Differential Diagnosis) with no page content provided (all 'content' fields empty). For radiology stations, need specific imaging atlases (e.g., 'Felson's Principles of Chest Roentgenology', 'ECG Made Easy Australia/NZ edition', 'RANZCR CT Head Interpretation Guidelines').
violations.recommendation: Use radiology-specific sources: RANZCR curricula, Australian imaging pathways (www.imagingpathways.health.wa.gov.au), RCH Clinical Practice Guidelines (Radiology), radiology teaching files.

violations.description: All stations allocated 8 minutes. For imaging interpretation OSCEs: CXR systematic review requires 5-6 minutes, ECG 12-lead analysis 4-5 minutes, CT head 6-7 minutes. If clinical management also required (as scenarios suggest), 8 minutes is insufficient.
violations.recommendation: Separate imaging interpretation (6 min) from clinical management (8 min) into distinct OSCE stations, OR extend combined stations to 12-15 minutes.

suggestions: Clarify station intent: Are these (A) Clinical assessment stations (history/examination/management) requiring clinical experts, OR (B) Imaging interpretation stations requiring actual radiological images?

If radiology interpretation intended: Replace all placeholder images with real radiological files (anonymized DICOM or high-resolution JPG/PNG). Example: ENDO-OSCE-0001 'Hyperthyroidism' could show thyroid ultrasound with heterogeneous echotexture + increased vascularity (Graves' disease), NOT 'Thyroid_Function_Tests' (laboratory).

For ECG stations (CARD-OSCE-0009 Syncope, CARD-OSCE-0012 Bradycardia, CARD-OSCE-0013 Long QT, CARD-OSCE-0019 Silent MI, GAST-OSCE-0041/0042 Hypo/Hyperkalemia): Provide actual 12-lead ECG images with calibration markers visible. Include clinical vignette (age, sex, presenting complaint) for correlation.

For CXR stations (CARD-OSCE-0018 Pulmonary Edema, GENE-OSCE-0027 Post-op SOB, GENE-OSCE-0028 Lung Cancer): Specify projection (PA/AP), inspiration (count anterior ribs visible), rotation (clavicular heads vs spinous processes), penetration (vertebrae visible behind heart).

For CT stations (GENE-OSCE-0028 Lung Cancer - CT Chest, GAST-OSCE-0035 Pancreatitis - CT Abdomen, NEUR-OSCE-0048 Headache - CT Brain, NEUR-OSCE-0049 Stroke - CT Brain): Provide axial slice images with window/level settings documented. Include scout image for anatomical orientation.
Add Australian radiological terminology glossary to OSCE instructions: 'consolidation' (not 'opacity'), 'pulmonary oedema' (not 'edema'), 'theatre' (not 'OR'), 'cannula' (not 'IV line').

Reference RANZCR curriculum (2023) for imaging appropriateness: Example - ENDO-OSCE-0003 DKA should NOT routinely have imaging (clinical + laboratory diagnosis); if imaging ordered, explain justification (? aspiration pneumonia, ? cerebral oedema).

For ultrasound stations (CARD-OSCE-0017 Upper Limb DVT, ENDO-OSCE-0006 Thyroid Nodules): Specify ultrasound technique (compression for DVT, Doppler for thyroid vascularity). Provide video clips or serial images, not single static frame.

Separate laboratory results from imaging: 'Thyroid_Function_Tests', 'ABG_Glucose', 'Cortisol_Tests', 'Hormone_Levels', 'ESR_CRP', 'Blood_Film', 'Blood_Culture', 'Electrolyte_Panel', 'Calcium_Level' are pathology (not radiology). Assign to pathology-interpretation-expert.

For 'clinical images' that are examination findings (ENDO-OSCE-0005 'Neurological_Exam', GENE-OSCE-0021 'Dermatological_Photo', CARD-OSCE-0010 'Assessment_Form'), assign to physical-examination-expert or clinical-documentation-expert.

If retaining as radiology stations, add structured reporting templates: CXR template (Indication, Technique [PA/AP, portable], Comparison, Findings [ABCDE], Impression), ECG template (Rate, Rhythm, Axis, Intervals, ST/T, Impression), CT template (Indication, Technique [contrast Y/N, slice thickness], Findings [ABC], Impression).

Include critical results notification protocol (ACSQHC National Safety and Quality Health Service Standards): Which findings require immediate phone call to referrer? (e.g., tension pneumothorax, free intraperitoneal air, STEMI on ECG, acute intracranial hemorrhage on CT).
strengths: Comprehensive topic coverage across multiple specialties (Endocrinology, Cardiology, Gastroenterology, Neurology) - 52 OSCEs spanning common clinical presentations.
RAG validation passed with confidence scores >0.65 for all references (metadata indicates 'rag_validation: PASSED').
Australian textbook sources included (John Murtagh General Practice - Australian GP standard text, AMC Handbook of Clinical Assessment).
Metadata well-structured with generation_date, total_osces, categories documented.
Time limit (8 minutes) appropriate for AMC Clinical Examination OSCE format.
agent_evaluations.manual_review_reason: CRITICAL SPECIALTY MISMATCH: This content is NOT radiology interpretation material. All 52 OSCEs are clinical assessment stations (history/examination/management) without actual radiological images to interpret. Contains placeholder image paths that do not exist, and 15/52 'image types' are non-radiological (laboratory tests, physical examination findings, clinical assessment forms). Cannot evaluate systematic radiology interpretation, image quality, or technical adequacy when no images provided. Recommend: (1) Assign to appropriate clinical experts (history-taking-expert, physical-examination-expert, clinical-documentation-expert, pathology-interpretation-expert); (2) If radiology interpretation intended, replace all placeholders with actual anonymized imaging files (DICOM/JPG of CXRs, ECGs, CTs) with technical parameters documented; (3) Clarify station objectives - currently ambiguous whether imaging interpretation or clinical management is being assessed.

violations.issue: No medication management content present in any OSCE scenarios
violations.suggested_fix: Add detailed medication management scenarios including: 1) Prescribing tasks with specific medications (drug name, dose, frequency, route, duration), 2) Medication reconciliation scenarios, 3) Adverse drug reaction management, 4) Drug interaction cases, 5) Therapeutic drug monitoring tasks

violations.issue: DKA scenario lacks insulin management protocol
violations.suggested_fix: Add insulin sliding scale protocol: Regular insulin IV infusion 0.1 unit/kg/hour, potassium replacement protocol (add KCl 40 mmol/L to IV fluids when K+ 3.3-5.3 mmol/L), fluid resuscitation (0.9% sodium chloride 1L over 1 hour, then adjust based on BP/urine output)

violations.issue: No medications specified - cannot verify Australian nomenclature compliance
violations.suggested_fix: When medications are added, ensure ALL use Australian names: paracetamol (NOT acetaminophen), adrenaline (NOT epinephrine), salbutamol (NOT albuterol), lignocaine (NOT lidocaine), GTN (NOT nitroglycerin)

violations.issue: No PBS codes or authority requirements documented
violations.suggested_fix: Add PBS compliance details for all prescriptions: PBS streamline codes, authority requirements (e.g., 'PBS authority required for >3 months continuous use'), specialist restrictions where applicable

violations.issue: Hypoglycemia scenario lacks specific glucose management protocol
violations.suggested_fix: Add: If conscious - 15g quick-acting carbohydrate (6 jelly beans OR 150mL fruit juice OR 3 glucose tablets), recheck BSL in 15 min. If unconscious - glucagon 1mg IM OR 10% dextrose 150-200mL IV (NOT 50% dextrose - tissue necrosis risk)

Add: Carbimazole 15-40mg daily PO (initial), then 5-15mg daily (maintenance). Beta-blocker for symptom control: Propranolol 40mg TDS PO OR metoprolol 50mg BD PO. Monitor: TFTs every 4-6 weeks until euthyroid, then 3-monthly. PBS authority required for carbimazole >6 months

violations.issue: Hypothyroidism scenario lacks levothyroxine dosing protocol
violations.suggested_fix: Add: Levothyroxine starting dose: 50-100 microgram daily PO (healthy adults), 25 microgram daily (elderly/cardiac disease). Take 30 min before breakfast. Titrate every 6-8 weeks based on TSH. Target TSH: 0.5-2.0 mIU/L. PBS unrestricted. Drug interactions: Iron, calcium, PPI reduce absorption (separate by 4 hours)

violations.issue: Warfarin management scenarios absent despite AF/VTE topics
violations.suggested_fix: Add warfarin scenario for AF (CARD-OSCE series): Target INR 2-3, drug interactions (warfarin + NSAIDs = contraindicated, warfarin + clarithromycin = ↑ INR, check INR 3-5 days after antibiotic), reversal protocol (INR >9: stop warfarin, vitamin K 1-2mg PO, recheck next day)

violations.issue: No elderly polypharmacy scenarios despite Fall Assessment OSCE
violations.suggested_fix: Add medication review task: Identify fall-risk medications (benzodiazepines, anticholinergics, antihypertensives causing postural hypotension), apply STOPP criteria (benzodiazepines ≥4 weeks in elderly = STOP), deprescribing plan

Add: Valaciclovir 1g TDS PO for 7 days (start within 72 hours of rash onset). Renal adjustment: eGFR 30-50 = 1g BD, eGFR 10-30 = 500mg BD. Analgesia: Paracetamol 1g QID + gabapentin 300mg nocte (titrate for neuropathic pain). PBS unrestricted if immunocompromised or age >50

violations.issue: Temporal Arteritis scenario lacks corticosteroid dosing
violations.suggested_fix: Add: Prednisolone 50-60mg daily PO (standard dose for GCA, higher if visual symptoms). Start IMMEDIATELY (do not wait for biopsy). Taper slowly over 12-18 months. Add: PPI for gastric protection (esomeprazole 20mg daily), calcium + vitamin D (osteoporosis prevention), bone density scan at baseline

violations.issue: Iron deficiency anemia scenario lacks oral iron preparation details
violations.suggested_fix: Add: Ferrous sulfate 325mg (105mg elemental iron) daily-BD PO. Take on empty stomach with vitamin C (enhances absorption). Side effects: Constipation, nausea, black stools. Recheck FBC + ferritin in 3 months. If intolerant: Ferrous fumarate OR IV iron (Ferinject 500-1000mg) if malabsorption/intolerance. Drug interaction: Iron + levothyroxine (separate by 4 hours)

violations.issue: OSA scenario should reference CPAP therapy, not medication, but ensure PAP terminology correct
violations.suggested_fix: Confirm Australian terminology: CPAP (continuous positive airway pressure), NOT 'BiPAP' (use 'bilevel PAP' in Australian practice). If pharmacotherapy discussed, use: Modafinil 100-200mg daily (excessive daytime sleepiness, PBS authority required)

To achieve medication-management-expert compliance: 1) Add specific medication tasks to each relevant OSCE (prescribing, monitoring, counseling), 2) Ensure 100% Australian drug nomenclature (paracetamol, adrenaline, salbutamol), 3) Include PBS codes and authority requirements, 4) Add renal/hepatic dosing adjustments where applicable, 5) Document drug interactions and contraindications, 6) Include therapeutic drug monitoring protocols for high-risk medications.
